content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as losing consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as cultures or liver and kidney function tests, may be conducted while you are taking this medication. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, and changes in taste. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking clarithromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin or azithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Clarithromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation, especially if you are using certain medications (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Clarithromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of clarithromycin from your body, which could impact how it works. Similarly, clarithromycin may slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as cultures or liver/kidney function tests) may be conducted while you are taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
